lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p1-2 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of number words. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.
“My grandmother has just turned 100! Is that a big number or a small number? Can you find your age on this page? Is that a big number or a small number?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p1-2 - B. Ask and Answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.
Look for accurate counting, correct use of ‘How many…?’ questions, clear numerical answers, and consistent reference to the objects in the picture.
“100 is a big number! Do you know what 100 of something looks like? How many of each item do you think there is in this picture?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p1-2 - C. Ask and Answer

details: Ask and answer provides the opportunity to use the target structure with personalised information.
Look for accurate use of ‘How old are you?’ and ‘I’m ___,’ appropriate number vocabulary, correct pronunciation, and natural turn-taking with classmates.
“Do you know how to ask a friend how old they are? Let’s practise together?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.101-102 - A Read and say

details: Read and say develops early decoding skills. Students blend sounds to read CVC words and practise recognising familiar phonics patterns before saying each word clearly and confidently.
Look for accurate blending, clear pronunciation, steady pacing, and correct identification of each word.
“It’s my birthday this weekend and, I really want a cat. And a pen. Can you help me write a list of everything I’d like?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.101-102 - A Find 5 sight words

details: Find 5 sight words strengthens recognition of high-frequency words. Students scan the wordsearch to locate words quickly and accurately, preparing them for fluent reading.
Look for correct identification of all five sight words, careful scanning, and accurate transfer to the writing lines.
“I know the sun isn’t something you can give! But I have a feeling the sun will come out if we can find all these words. Will you help me?”

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Write gives students controlled practice spelling the sight words they located. It reinforces whole-word memory, letter order, and neat handwriting.
Look for correct spelling, consistent letter formation, and neat handwriting within the lines.
